Title: Simple tourny rules to replace restricted list

Messages.Author: Alec Habig
Messages.Body:
It looks to me like the following simple rules would render the need for the
restricted list as outlined in the recent DC rules. To wit:

1) Play vote pushing as written in the Jyad rules - "other Meths may burn PA
cards in exchange for votes" (paraphrased).

(That addresses all the political cards on the list)

2) A vampire may not attempt the same action more than once per turn.

(This addresses all the untap abuses)

That leaves only 5th tradition - it's the only one that doesn't directly fit
into #1 or #2.

I contend that without untap abuse, 5th tradition is merely a good card, rather
than an abusive one, but just in case :

3) 5th tradition is not usable on a prince or justicar.

A question for Tom -

You are the net.liason. You do a great job of communicating WotC news to us,
the net reading public. However, liason is a two-way street. How successful
are you at communicating the ideas proposed here to the design team/DC people?

One cancellation of a previous ruling, one rules addendum, and one card errata,
three lines in all, seem a lot more elegant than card limits.

Alec

Messages.Author: Charles T. Schwope
Messages.Body:
Thomas R Wylie (aa...@cats.ucsc.edu) wrote:

: Alec Habig <aha...@bigbang.astro.indiana.edu> wrote:
: >A question for Tom -
: >You are the net.liason. You do a great job of communicating WotC news to us,
: >the net reading public. However, liason is a two-way street. How successful
: >are you at communicating the ideas proposed here to the design team/DC people?

: Apparently not as successful as I thought, given the 2-per-card limit
: on the restricted list. But I am, more or less, in charge of the rules team.

Its nice to see that you were against the "2 limit."
The internet should be seen by the DC as a huge playtest group.
And currently there are 2 basic opinions: use a 4 card limit, or use no
limits but have some sort of house rules/errata to fix the restricted
cards. This resource is not being effectively utilized by the DC, b/c
despite all the playtesting done at WoTC, the internet community does
much more.
The tourney rules have failed to make anyone happy, and most
likely will never be widely used. This is a shame, b/c its the tourneys
that have made MtG the huge success that it is. And now this won't
happen with VTES.

: >One cancellation of a previous ruling, one rules addendum, and one card errata

: >three lines in all, seem a lot more elegant than card limits.

: The DC is not in the business of altering the gameplay of the card games
: it has tournament rules for. Deck construction, yes, but the only modification
: to gameplay has been Ring of Ma'Ruf. Gameplay is left up to R&D.

You can't honestly believe this is true. If the tournament
format becomes readily accepted by people then it basicly reflects
the rules of the game. No one plays MtG with more then 4 or a card
in their deck, b/c the tourney rules are the standard. The main reason
for this is the fact that MtG is a broken game without limits. Jyhad,
on the other hand, basicly isn't. This is the main reason why the
tourney rules will never be accepted: 1st off they are bad, and 2nd
Jyhad is not a broken game without them.
Did the DC playtest decks under the rules they proposed? Not
likely. Does the DC want variety in the decks that people play at
tourneys? Obviously not. Right now every tournament will be a
competition of who can put together the best stealth-bleed deck.
Who can afford the best rares for their decks, who gets the right
distribution of cards.
What happens when it becomes obvious that the only way to win
a tournament is to use S-B. Will they restrict the Dominate bleed
boosters? Or will they restrict Malkavians? (Yes, your crypt can only
have one Malkavian in it, b/c those damn Malks are just so much better
at what you have to do to win one of our tourneys.) Or will Malk
Dementia become restricted, b/c everyone is using it?

I think the best solution for this is to have the internet players
get together and make their own set of tourney rules. Have one or two
of the most vocal supporters of given view points (aka limit vs no limit)
talk over email, and come to some sort of compromise that players of
both limit and non-limit Jyhad can play . Then post what they come up
with to the net, and get some feedback. Make any needed changes, then
re-posst, etc. It really should take that long. Then there would be a
standard that can be spread. Who knows, the DC might get a clue and pay
attention when they realize that no one is willing to use their rules.
Actually, I'll volunteer to be the "center contact" or arbitrator if
people are willing to do this.
